title: Genitiv
theme: Nema kahve. English of is a separate word here.
reviewerNotes: Bosnian editor pass. Genitive forms check out (kahve, kuće, mosta, piva, Sarajeva, Emira, auta, mora; nema/iz/od/ispred/još/šolja + gen; tri kahve). whyHere.heading: Why you are here
whyHere.body: Today you learn the of, from, and none job on the same coffee you already filed and wanted. Amira can say Nema kahve when the pot is empty, and that e is not the want-it u from Chapter 2. English hangs of and from in front as separate words. Bosnian hangs the job on the end again. You get one new outfit on the same small word set.

englishLies.heading: Why English lies
englishLies.body: English lies because a cup of coffee, coffee from Sarajevo, and there is no coffee keep the word coffee still. You only add little words in front. Bosnian moves the ending instead. Kahva becomes kahve in that job. Schools call the job genitiv. You can keep saying of, from, and none and still be right. The pile stays whatever you filed in Chapter 1. Only the job mark changes.

knownLine.heading: A line you already say
knownLine.body: Book 1 already put Emir in Sarajevo with iz Sarajeva, and it already let Ana want more coffee with Želim još kahve. Today those endings get a name. The café line that shows this job is Amira’s Nema kahve, which means there is no coffee. Kahve is still the she-word. It is not kahvu. Wanting the drink and having none of it are different jobs.
knownLine.speaker: Amira

pattern.heading: The pattern
pattern.body: She-pile words swap that final a for e in the of, from, and none job. Kahva becomes kahve, and kuća becomes kuće. He-pile words usually add a, so most becomes mosta and auto becomes auta. Leftover-pile words usually turn the last o or e into a, so pivo becomes piva and Sarajevo becomes Sarajeva. Use that form after nema, after iz and od, and when English would say of. Learn kahve first. Then notice mosta and piva follow their own pile habits.

howYouGuess.heading: The pests
howYouGuess.body: Three pests will trip you today. The first is saying Nema kahva, which leaves coffee in the name-it form when you mean none. The second is grabbing kahvu because Chapter 2 trained your hand for wanting. Kahvu is want-it. Kahve is of, from, and none. The third pest is Emira. You already saw Emira for I see Emir. The same shape often appears for of Emir or from Emir. People in the he pile reuse that look. A bridge does not reuse that look. Most becomes mosta when you mean of the bridge.

trick.heading: The bit that tricks you
trick.body: The trap is to treat every moved ending as the want-it job. Kahvu and kahve are neighbors, not twins. Ana wants kahvu. Amira has none of kahve. The other trap is to translate English of as a free word you can drop in front of the list form. Šolja kahva is wrong. Šolja kahve puts the of job on the coffee itself. If you keep the list form after nema, iz, or of, you sound like you never changed jobs.

nerd.heading: Why it's like this
nerd.body:
Old English is the English of England about a thousand years ago, not a class you missed. Farmers and priests around Winchester marked of and from on the end of a thing-word. A scrap survived in later English as the possessive s on names, and as of sitting in front. You speak the later version, so coffee itself stays still while of does the work.

Bosnian never fired that older habit on kahva. The e on kahve is a leftover job mark from the same family as name-it and want-it. Schools call the whole family case. Today you only add the of, from, and none job. Tomorrow’s jobs are to, at, and about on the same coffee.

items.prompt: Amira has no coffee. Which form?
items.explanation: Nema takes the of and none form, so the right word is kahve.
Want-it from Chapter 2 is still kahvu. Do not steal today’s e for wanting.

items.prompt: Emir is from Sarajevo. Which form after iz?
items.explanation: Iz takes the of and from form. Leftover Sarajevo becomes Sarajeva.

items.prompt: There is no beer. Which form?
items.explanation: Nema piva. Leftover o became a.

items.prompt: Roof of the house. Which form of kuća?
items.explanation: She-pile a became e for the of job.

items.prompt: There is no bridge. Which form?
items.explanation: He-pile things add a here, so the right word is mosta.

items.prompt: Someone says Nema kahva. What went wrong?
options: They left coffee in the name-it form.
items.explanation: Nema needs kahve. Kahva only names it.

items.prompt: Želim još kahve uses which job on coffee?
items.explanation: Još takes the of form. The wanting is already in želim.

items.prompt: Od Emira. Why does Emira look familiar?
options: It switched to the she pile.
He-pile people often share this look with the want-it job.
items.explanation: Vidim Emira and od Emira can look the same. Mosta is the bridge’s separate of form.

items.prompt: English of is a separate word. What does Bosnian do?
options: Keeps kahva and adds of in front
Puts the of job on the ending
items.explanation: Šolja kahve. The ending carries of.

questions.question: Tri kahve, molim. Why kahve?
questions.explanation: After tri, coffee takes the of-and-none form kahve. Same shelf as nema kahve.

questions.question: Nema kahve uses which form?
options: Of and none form on the same she-word
questions.explanation: Kahva became kahve. The pile stayed she.

questions.question: She-pile words like kahva and kuća usually do what in this job?
questions.explanation: Kahve and kuće. The u was yesterday’s want-it mark.

questions.question: Why is Ja sam iz Sarajeva correct?
options: Sarajevo is she, so it takes e
Iz takes the of and from form, and leftover Sarajevo becomes Sarajeva
questions.explanation: Book 1 already used that line. Today you know why the ending moved.

questions.question: Why is Nema kahvu the wrong café line?
options: Because kahvu is the want-it job, not the none job
Because nema needs the name-it form
questions.explanation: Wanting is kahvu. None is kahve.

questions.question: There is no car. Which form after nema?
questions.explanation: Nema takes the of/none form. Pest auto still follows he habits, so auta.

next.body: You now know why Nema kahve is not Nema kahva, and why kahvu stays in the want-it column. Iz Sarajeva and šolja kahve use the same of job. Chapter 4 is giving, liking, and in versus into on the same small set. You still will not get a seven-job chart.
